openings.claim: Probe reversible attachment feasibility before shifting sideways-load carriage from seal friction to padded strip contacts: two removable rim saddles using four strips, six bolt/nut sets, four pads and cord retaining removed assemblies outside the opening. This is a probe, not deployment.
openings.discriminator: Lateral registration predicts at most 1 mm displacement under 20 N without added corner lift or slower reopening. Nearest rival, stronger retention supplying sufficient friction, needs additional restraint. Geometry may defeat either account. Balanced pressure remains an untested alternative, not a contradictory prediction about this joint.
openings.probe: Inspect rim access, strip span, pad placement and external tether clearance without loading the seal; park fabrication if removable attachment or unobstructed opening is unsupported. Fabricate within ninety minutes; conduct ten numbered opening/closure/pull cycles within twenty minutes using ruler, scale and stopwatch, placing the supplied 1 mm card at the marked right contact for final closure. Record marked displacement, corner heights, reopening time, tears and maintenance. Reject acceptance for displacement above 1 mm, failed 20 N retention, reopening above thirty seconds, tears, permanent deformation, unrecoverable parts or obstructed full inspection opening. Waive only disturbed seal-contact continuity. Stop for damage; stopping supplies no feasibility evidence. No drilling, cutting, gluing or permanent deformation of hatch/trough; use no powered mechanism. Retain existing hatch, rim and seal.
openings.uncertainty: Rim geometry, pad behavior, strip stiffness and tether attachment are unspecified. Technician operation/recording within the allowance is assumed; borderline ruler readings remain uncertain. Ten cycles validate only one configuration; no causal winner follows.

lineage.reason: Preserves causal carrier, rival and defeat conditions, feasibility gate, coupled acceptance, stopping/resource caveats and declared uncertain fit.

decision: Check attachment feasibility first. At most two configurations and twelve closure/pull trials, including a disturbed trial per configuration, cannot establish ten-cycle outcomes for both. Passing supports further evaluation only; pressure redistribution versus geometry remains unresolved; agreement supplies no evidence.
